lines.junior: Mrs. Lee's tea house had been keeping Eleanor's red tin, with a rabbit under a full moon. You made Eleanor's tea the 1926 way and earned it. Mei Lee's diary revealed the Lark's secret: its six-note song is split into two halves. The tin opened with 4, 2, 4 and pointed you to a brass bird on the Brooklyn Bridge. Dexter and Nora overheard everything.
lines.master: Mrs. Lee's tea house had safeguarded Eleanor's red tin, adorned with a rabbit under a full moon. By brewing Eleanor's tea the 1926 way, you earned it. Mei Lee's diary disclosed the Lark's secret: its six-note song is divided into two halves. The tin yielded to 4, 2, 4 and directed you to a brass bird on the Brooklyn Bridge. Dexter and Nora overheard every word.

Today my friend Eleanor left her red tin with me.
She told me a secret about her Lark.
It sings a song of six notes.
She put the first three notes on a brass bird.
The last three notes stay with her own family.
"Only my whole song wakes my Lark," she said.

lines.rookie: Under the first stone tower, a brass bird sits on a bench.
lines.junior: Beneath the first stone tower, a brass bird sits on a bench.
lines.master: Beneath the first stone tower, a brass bird is perched on a bench.

lines.rookie: Wonderful! We'll film there tomorrow!
lines.junior: Fantastic! We'll film there tomorrow!
lines.master: Splendid! We'll shoot there tomorrow!

lines.rookie: The bird holds the song's first three notes.
lines.junior: The first three notes of the song are on the bird.
lines.master: The bird carries the first three notes of the song.

lines.rookie: Sorry... I have to go now.
lines.junior: Sorry... I need to leave now.
lines.master: Forgive me... I really must go.

lines.rookie: Why does Nora look so worried?
lines.junior: Why does Nora seem so worried?
lines.master: Why does Nora appear so troubled?
